To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) proteins EBNA3A (encoded by EBV gene BHLF1) and EBNA3B (encoded by EBNA3B) are required for the expression of the oncogenic microRNA (miRNA) cluster miR-221 and miR-222, which is expressed at high level in human tumours and is a target of multiple tumour suppressors.
EBNA3 proteins are necessary to activate the oncogenic miRNA cluster miR-221/222 in B cells and to inhibit expression of the tumour suppressive miRNA cluster miRNA143/145.

EBNA3 proteins are required for the expression of the oncogenic microRNA (miRNA) cluster miR-221/ miR-222 and that the EBV-encoded proteins EBNA3A, EBNA3C, and EBNA3B are necessary to repress the tumour suppressive miRNA cluster miR-145/miR-143 in EBV-infected cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role played by Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) in the development of B cell lymphoma and leukaemia.
the molecular basis of the Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated lymphomas.
understanding how EBV proteins contribute to the oncogenic process, and how the virus manipulates host cell gene expression programmes to promote its own replication.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EBNA3 proteins are necessary for the expression of miR-222/221, and the repression of miR-143/145.
EBV-encoded EBNA3A/EBNA3C proteins induce oncogenic miR clusters and repress tumour suppressor miRs.
the EBV-encoded EBNA3 proteins are able to manipulate host gene expression by targeting both host protein-coding genes and host miRs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

EBNA3 proteins are involved in the regulation of host gene expression at many levels, including the transcription of host genes, the regulation of miR expression, and also by the direct binding to and modification of the host chromatin.
EBV-encoded proteins can manipulate the transcription of host genes by direct binding to chromatin and by long-range interactions with host transcription factors.

the EBNA3A/EBNA3C proteins, in addition to repressing a large number of cellular protein-coding genes, also repress a large number of tumour suppressive miRNAs, and activate a large number of oncoprotein-activating miRNAs, thus creating a cellular microRNA profile which is conducive to B-cell proliferation and transformation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Epstein-Barr virus-encoded EBNA3A/3C transcription factors are necessary for activation of the oncogenic microRNA cluster miR-221/222 and repression of the tumour suppressive miR-143/145 cluster in B cells.
EBNA3s are able to manipulate host gene expression at multiple levels and that this may be an important aspect of their oncogenic activity.

EBV has developed a sophisticated mechanism to regulate the expression of miRs that are involved in cell transformation, and that these EBV proteins can be used to target specific miRs for therapeutic purposes in the future.
